paragraphs.text: Cozlin looked at all the cameras. "Cool! I'm going to be on TV!"
The show's host, Tark Zeldo, walked over. "Kid Comet! I'm glad you're here. We'll have a wonderful interview."
Cozlin and Tark sat down.
Tark looked at a camera. "Good morning, Delkor! Kid Comet is with me to talk about her life as a superhero. So, Kid Comet, what's it like being so powerful?"
Cozlin shrugged. "It's not a big deal—to me, at least. I've been powerful for my entire life!"
"You have a pretty big job, keeping us safe all by yourself," Tark said. "Do you ever wish Delkor had more superheroes?"
Cozlin snorted. "I don't need help."
Tark's device beeped. "Oh! I'm getting some breaking news . . . A big robot's invading our city!"
Cozlin waved a hand. "I'll be right back, Tark!"
Zoom! Cozlin was gone in a flash. Downtown, she saw Delkorians running all over. Smoke rose from an intersection, and a big robot crushed a bus. Crunch!
Zap! Lasers shot from Cozlin's hand, destroying the robot. Ka-boom!
Cozlin laughed. "What a junky—" Another robot threw a car at her.
Zap! Cozlin blasted that robot. But then another robot appeared and smashed a police car.
"Kid Comet!" a voice cried. It was Detective Borzon. He was hiding behind a tree with several other Delkorians.
Cozlin hurried over. "Is that your car, Detective? It looks great! I like all the dents."
The detective frowned. "Ha-ha. This is serious, Kid Comet."
Cozlin shrugged. "I know it seems serious, Detective. But I can handle it." She scratched her head. "I'm confused though. Tark Zeldo said there was one robot. I've seen three."
"At first there was one," someone said. "But—"
"Look!" Detective Borzon pointed.

Cozlin spun around. One of the robots ate a car. Strange sounds came from inside the robot. Then a hatch popped open on the back of the robot. A new robot popped out! Down the street she saw another robot eat a car and make a new robot.
Cozlin flew high into the air. She looked down and gasped. Robots were everywhere!
"I'm mad!" Roxy said.
Roxy and her friends were walking home from school, talking about their day. During recess an older kid had made fun of Terrell for wearing glasses.
"I was mad too," Mara said. "But at least he apologized."
"He seemed pretty sorry," Jack said.
Roxy frowned. "He only apologized because he got in trouble. A teacher had to talk to him first."
Terrell shrugged. "It's not a big deal, Roxy."
Jack and Mara turned left to go to their homes. Roxy and Terrell walked together.
"I don't think you should forgive the kid, Terrell," Roxy said. "When people are bad, they're always bad."
"That sounds kind of harsh," Terrell said.
"Remember Dr. Odd, the robot maker?"
Terrell nodded.
"He was just released from prison for good behavior," Roxy said. "But there's no way he's a good guy now."
"Maybe he changed," Terrell said.
"No way," Roxy repeated. "It's only a matter of time before he commits more crimes."
Just then Roxy's watch beeped. "Mayor Bloom! What's wrong?"
The mayor looked scared. "We need help, Rocket Girl! There's a huge monster in downtown Metro City!"
Roxy looked at Terrell. "I have to stop that monster."
"See you later," Terrell mumbled before walking away.
"That's odd," Roxy thought. "Terrell seems annoyed. I wonder why." She sighed. "I can't think about that now."
A moment later she was flying over the city.
Roar! An enormous monster stood between several tall buildings.
"Whoa!" Roxy said. "That monster is huge!"
In the streets below, people ran in every direction.
"Look out!" a taxi driver shouted.
"Run for your lives!" a construction worker yelled.
Crash! Two cars hit each other. Roxy flew down fast.
"Is everyone okay?" she asked.
One driver gave her a thumbs-up. "I'm fine!" she said. "This car was old anyway."
The other driver frowned. "Ugh! I spilled a mango smoothie all over myself!" He sighed. "But I'm okay."
"Rocket Girl!" Detective Smith shouted.
Roxy saw the detective hiding behind a hot dog stand. She flew over to him.
"Hi, Detective!" Roxy said. "I didn't know you worked at a hot dog stand."
The detective frowned. "Very funny, Rocket Girl."
"Do you know where the monster came from?" Roxy asked.
"I have no idea," Detective Smith said.
The hot dog stand owner popped up from behind the stand. "It just appeared suddenly!"
"Huh?" Roxy said.
"Everything was fine," the owner said. "Until I looked down to get a hot dog for a customer. When I looked back up, that monster was here!"
Roar! The monster walked down the street as cars and buses swerved to avoid being hit.
"Wait here, Detective!" Roxy flew after the enormous monster. "Hey! Stop right there!"

The monster didn't seem to hear her. It kept walking slowly. Roxy got ready to fire her eye laser beams. But then a bus turned too fast and flipped over. Roxy shot back down to the street and lifted the bus back onto its wheels.
"Thanks, Rocket Girl!" The bus driver slammed on the gas pedal and sped away.

Roxy flew back up and saw the enormous monster swatting at helicopters. One helicopter swerved, and its tail bumped a building. The tail broke, smoke poured out, and the helicopter began to spiral down.
"Yikes!" Roxy shot through the air and grabbed the helicopter with both hands.
"Grr!" Roxy struggled to slow the helicopter down. Finally she brought it down safely in Metro City Park.
The pilot wiped sweat from his forehead. "Thanks, Rocket Girl!"
Roxy smiled. "No problem."

She quickly flew back downtown. The monster headed down a wide street. As Roxy followed it, she noticed something odd. "That monster is moving silently," she thought. "I don't hear any stomping." Then she gasped. The monster's paw seemed to go right through a building. But the building looked fine.
Roxy scratched her head. "Is the monster a hologram?"
The monster was now walking toward the mountains outside the city. She followed it out of the city. Blink! It disappeared.
Confused, Roxy looked all around. Then she saw a familiar alien superhero nearby.
"Kid Comet!" Roxy shouted.
Cozlin grinned. "Hey, Rocket Girl!"

Cozlin smiled. "That monster was cool, right?" She held up a controller. "This can make any hologram I want." She pressed a button, causing a huge octopus to appear. Cozlin played with the buttons on the controller. A tidal wave rose from the ground, and then a spaceship zoomed toward them. Roxy ducked to avoid getting hit.
"They're not real!" Laughing, Cozlin made everything vanish.
Roxy glared at her. "Why did you make that monster? That was dangerous!"
Cozlin shrugged. "It didn't hurt anyone."
"No," Roxy said, "but people were scared!"
Cozlin rolled her eyes. "I needed to find you. I looked all over and realized I had no idea where you might be. But then I said to myself, 'A big monster will get Rocket Girl's attention!'"
Cozlin chuckled. Roxy frowned.
"Okay." Cozlin held up her hands. "Maybe it wasn't a good idea. But King Radnik said I needed your help."
"Who's King Radnik?" Roxy asked.
"The king of Delkor," Cozlin said. "A robot army is invading our planet, and he's really worried. So he insisted I ask you for help. I told him all about you after the first time I was here."
"A robot army sounds serious," Roxy said.
Cozlin shrugged. "I'm sure I can handle it. And I'm sure you have other things to do."
Roxy sighed. "I'd be happy to help you. But I don't know if I should leave Earth. What if someone robs a bank? What if huge bugs suddenly swarm the city? My city needs me."
Just then Roxy's watch beeped. Usually only Roxy could hear it, but Cozlin looked down at it too.
"What's that?" Cozlin asked.
"It's an emergency," Roxy said. She flipped open the watch. All she could see was darkness. "Mayor Bloom! What's wrong? Mayor Bloom?"
Mayor Bloom's face suddenly appeared, looking confused. "Rocket Girl? Is everything okay? Did you get rid of that monster?"
"Yep!" Roxy said. "Is that why you called?"
"I didn't call you," Mayor Bloom said.
"Um, you did, Mayor," Roxy said.
"I did?" Mayor Bloom chuckled. "Oops. I guess I sat on my phone."
Roxy sighed. "So, nothing's wrong?"
"Nope!" Mayor Bloom smiled. "I'm just organizing my desk."
Roxy closed her watch. "Kid Comet, I'll go with you."
"Are you sure?" Cozlin asked. "I can just tell King Radnik you were busy."
"No," Roxy said. "You need my help, so I'll help you. But promise me that you'll never scare the people of Metro City like that again."
"I promise. I don't think this will take long at all—probably just an hour or two. In fact, I could easily handle it on my own. But with your help, it'll get done faster," Cozlin said.
Roxy gave Cozlin a funny look. "You know, there's nothing wrong with needing help."
Cozlin shrugged. "I like to work alone."
They got into Cozlin's spaceship and blasted off. A power crystal in the control panel glowed brightly, and soon they were approaching Delkor.
The spaceship flew over Delkor's capital. Looking down, both Roxy and Cozlin gasped. The entire city was filled with robots!
Roxy looked at the city streets below. She saw lines of robots moving about like ants in a colony.
Cozlin bit her lip. Roxy could tell she was scared.
"This is fine!" Cozlin said suddenly. "We can definitely handle it." She flew the spaceship close to a large building covered in robots, and gulped.
"What is that place?" Roxy asked.
"King Radnik's palace." Cozlin picked up a communication device. "This is Kid Comet! I'm trying to reach King Radnik."
There was no answer.
"Uh-oh," Roxy thought.
Finally a voice came through the communication device. "King Radnik is in an underground bunker. I'll send you the location."
Cozlin let out a huge sigh of relief.
Soon the spaceship arrived at two large metal doors in the side of a grassy hill. The doors opened, and the spaceship flew in.
"I'm glad you're back, Kid Comet!" King Radnik said. He looked at Roxy. "Thank you for coming. Those robots are causing a lot of trouble."
"I'm happy to help, King, um, Your Majesty," Roxy said.
They went into a meeting room where a screen displayed a map of the capital. Government officials hurried back and forth.
"We're planning an evacuation," King Radnik said. "I want every Delkorian off the planet as fast as possible. And I want to know where those robots came from. Who sent them? Why are they here?"
Cozlin nodded. "I'll figure it out!"
"We both will," Roxy said.
Cozlin glanced at her. "Right! We both will."
Cozlin landed her spaceship just outside the city. Roxy watched the robots move around the streets. Every robot had the letter M stamped on it.
"I wonder what that M stands for," Roxy said.
"Who cares," Cozlin said. Zap! She blasted a robot.
Whiz-hoo! Roxy's eye laser beams blew apart another robot.
One robot pointed at Roxy and Cozlin. "Destroy them!"
Robots stomped toward the two superheroes.
"Uh-oh!" Roxy flew fast. She darted away from one robot and smashed another.
Cozlin zipped back and forth, blasting robots that tried to grab her.
As Roxy flew, she saw a robot chomping on a vehicle. The robot hummed and then another robot popped out of its back.
Whiz-hoo! She blasted the first robot, and it blew up. Then Roxy gasped. The second robot fell over, lifeless.
Cozlin saw it too. "Rocket Girl!" she said. "We need to destroy the first robot that came here! Then maybe all the others will stop working!"
The two of them blasted one robot after another. But it didn't seem to help. Robots were still everywhere!
Roxy and Cozlin were exhausted. They flew out of the city and flopped on the ground.
"This is awful!" Cozlin said. "What am I going to do?"
"You mean, what are we going to do," Roxy said. "Don't forget—you dragged me into this. You said it would just take an hour or two!"
Cozlin sat up suddenly. "Did you hear that?"
Roxy scratched her head. "Huh?"
"Someone's here," Cozlin said.
Roxy saw an alien peeking over a nearby boulder. He gasped, ran to a scooter, and zoomed away.
Roxy watched the alien zoom away on the scooter.
"He's controlling the robots!" she shouted.
Cozlin looked angry. "Let's get him!"
The alien glanced over his shoulder. "Oh no!" His scooter shot forward with incredible speed.
Roxy and Cozlin chased the alien as he zipped back and forth between large boulders. He soon arrived at a clearing where other aliens stood near a spaceship.
"They're not Delkorians," Cozlin said.
Roxy and Cozlin approached them.
"Who are you?" Cozlin asked, looking stern.
An alien stepped forward. "Please don't hurt us! My name is Eldin, and we're from the planet Trell."
"What are you doing on Delkor?" Cozlin asked.
"We've been flying through space," Eldin said, "looking for a new home."
Cozlin narrowed her eyes. "And you thought you could use those robots to take over Delkor! Then you could make it your new home!"
Eldin's eyes went wide. "Absolutely not! We were trying to get away from the robots on Trell. We didn't realize one was on our spaceship. It must have sneaked on while we were evacuating Trell."
"It wasn't just one robot," Roxy said. "There are lots of them!"

Eldin shook his head. "There was only one robot on board our spaceship. It found the ship's controls and crashed the ship here. Our mechanics are now trying to fix our ship." He sighed. "We are so sorry for bringing that robot here."
Cozlin chuckled. "Don't feel too bad, Eldin. The robots are annoying, but I can handle them."
Roxy frowned. "You mean, we can handle them."

"I doubt you can stop them," Eldin said. "That's why we had to flee Trell. Those robots took over our entire planet in just a couple of weeks. And Trell wasn't the first planet they invaded. They've taken over other planets, and once they invade, they quickly make more robots. There's no way to stop them."
Roxy gulped and looked at Cozlin. "I have to help her," Roxy thought. "Her entire planet is in danger."
"Do you know where the robots first came from?" Cozlin asked Eldin.
"No," Eldin said.
Cozlin turned to Roxy. "I have a plan. Let's go."
Roxy and Cozlin said good-bye to the Trellians and headed back toward the city.
"We have to find the original robot," Cozlin said. "If we destroy it, all the others will stop working."
"We tried that," Roxy said. "We don't know which one is the original."

"The original probably isn't here," Cozlin said. "You heard Eldin's story. Those robots have invaded other planets. We have to get a good look at the technology the robots use. Then we can figure out where they came from."
"Good idea!" Roxy said. "Let's get one of the robots we destroyed."
Roxy and Cozlin flew back to the city. By now all the vehicles were gone, but robots were still everywhere.
"The robots must have turned all the vehicles into other robots," Cozlin said.
"That's not all they did," Roxy said. "Look around . . . There are no more broken robots. They must have turned them into new robots as well!"
Roxy groaned. "We destroyed so many robots. And now they've all been fixed! It's like we didn't do anything at all!"
Roxy felt bad. She wanted to help the Delkorians, but this mission was taking a really long time.
Cozlin held up her hand. Zap!
One robot exploded, and three others fell over, lifeless. Roxy flew over and grabbed one of the lifeless robots. She and Cozlin took it into their spaceship.
"Let's get this robot to the bunker," Cozlin said. "An expert can study its technology and figure out where it came from."
They flew back to the bunker. But now the grassy hill was covered in large pieces of metal. Robots were welding the pieces of metal together.
"What are they doing?" Roxy asked.
"I don't know," Cozlin said. "But we can't get into the bunker now." She turned on her communication device. "This is Kid Comet. Is everyone okay inside the bunker?"
"Yes," a voice said. "What's going on out there?"
"Robots covered the entrance," Cozlin said. "We can't get in."
"Maybe we can get help in a different city," Roxy said.
"Every city on Delkor has been overrun by robots," the voice said. "No place is safe!"
Cozlin gulped. "Don't worry! We'll stop them."
"She's scared," Roxy thought.
Just then a robot jumped onto the outside of their ship. It punched into a wing and tried to pull it apart.
"Oh no!" Cozlin shouted.
Roxy flew outside. She knocked the robot off the wing. Using her heat vision, she quickly welded the wing back together. Then more robots tried to attack the ship.
Roxy went back inside, and Cozlin flew up into orbit.
"It's not safe down there," Roxy said. "How will we figure out where the robots came from?"

Cozlin was pressing buttons on the dashboard. "My aunt Fezlin is a technology researcher. She lives on Asteroid Number 4. It's a huge asteroid that orbits Delkor's star. We can see if she knows anything about the robots."
The power crystal glowed, and the spaceship shot through space. Minutes later Cozlin's spaceship was docking on Asteroid Number 4.
"I'm even farther from Earth now," Roxy thought.
Aunt Fezlin hugged Cozlin. "I've been hearing reports about what's happening on Delkor. I'm glad you're safe, Cozlin."
Cozlin looked at Roxy and shrugged. "That's my real name."
Roxy smiled. "Mine is Roxy."
"It's nice to meet you, Roxy," Aunt Fezlin said. "Cozlin acts like she never needs help, but everyone needs a teammate sometimes."
Cozlin shrugged. "Roxy isn't a teammate. She's just helping me."
"That's right," Roxy said, pretending to agree. "Cozlin doesn't even need my help. In fact, maybe I should just go home to my own—"
"Sorry!" Cozlin said quickly. "Please don't go—I do need your help."
Roxy smiled. "I'll stay."
Aunt Fezlin examined the robot, taking it apart. She looked closely at how it had been built.
"This technology is from the Varda Region," she said finally.
"Then that's where we need to go," Cozlin said.
Roxy had a sinking feeling. "How far away is that?"
Cozlin shrugged. "About a million light-years."
Roxy sighed. "This mission is taking me farther and farther from home!"
"Stop complaining, Roxy," Cozlin said as they took off. "A million light-years sounds far, but we have a Delkorian power crystal. So the trip will actually be pretty quick."
"Okay," Roxy said, yawning.
They took a short nap in the spaceship's sleeping pods. When they woke up, they were passing by a huge nebula. An hour later they reached the Varda Region.
Cozlin pressed a button, and a map appeared.
"The spaceship's computer knows the location of every object in the region," Cozlin said. She leaned closer. "Hmm. Something is wrong with one of the planets."
Roxy saw that one planet—a bright green one—was blinking on the map.
Cozlin tapped the planet, causing it to expand.

"Planet Groon," a voice said. "Located in the Varda Region, Groon is a forest planet with a large population. The entire surface is covered in trees. Groonians spend much of their time growing fruit trees."
"That sounds like a nice place," Roxy said.
"Yep," Cozlin said. "But not anymore. The sensors aren't picking up any signs of life!"
They flew to Groon and didn't see anything green at all. Instead, metal structures, along with parts from spaceships and other machines, covered the surface.
"It's as if the entire planet has been turned into a big junkyard!" Roxy said.
"It's been overrun by robots," Cozlin said. "Maybe the robots on Delkor came from here."
In the distance they saw a small sphere stuck to the planet.
"That looks like a moon," Roxy said.
They landed near the sphere and stepped outside.
Roxy's feet clinked on the metal surface. "I can't believe there was once a forest under here."
Cozlin nodded but didn't say anything. Roxy knew why.
"She's scared this will happen to Delkor," Roxy thought. "I know I'm far from home. But this is where I need to be right now. Cozlin needs me!"
They walked past all sorts of strange objects. Some looked like rockets or satellites. Others appeared to be vehicles or just scraps of metal.
"Where did all of this come from?" Roxy said.
Cozlin shrugged. "Other planets?"
They found an entrance with a walkway that went down into the planet.
As Roxy examined the metal surrounding the entrance, she gasped. "Here's an M , just like on all the robots back on Delkor!"
"Wow," Cozlin said. "Then we really are in the right place. Let's go in!" She took out a device. "This can detect life. If anyone is in here, we'll know."

They went down the walkway. Cozlin's device beeped regularly as it scanned the environment. Up ahead, Roxy saw something strange. A shimmering energy shield filled the corridor. She could see that the corridor continued on the other side of the shield.
Cozlin stuck her hand through the energy shield. She shrugged. "I think it's safe."
They stepped through it and continued to walk. Cozlin's device wasn't beeping anymore.
Roxy glanced over. "I think your device stopped—"
"Uh-oh!" Cozlin said, pointing ahead. Roxy looked and saw three mean-looking robots.
"I'll get them!" Roxy tried to fire her eye laser beams, but nothing happened.
"Oh no!" Roxy cried. "I don't have my super powers!"
Roxy looked at the robots. "Cozlin! Do something!"
Cozlin held up her hand, but nothing happened. "I don't have my super powers either!"
The robots moved closer. Cozlin grabbed Roxy and pulled her into a small opening in the wall.
"Follow me!" Cozlin said.
They crawled through a narrow tunnel. It was too small for any of those robots to enter. The floor was slippery with thick, dark sludge.
"There's something on the floor," Roxy said.
"It's motor oil," Cozlin said. "Maybe oil drains into this tunnel."
"Yuck!" Roxy said.
They reached a small chamber and stood up.
"That was close," Cozlin said.
Roxy frowned. "We're covered in motor oil!"
Cozlin shrugged. "At least we're safe now."
"Safe?" Roxy said. "Are you kidding? We're trapped in a tunnel a million light-years from home without super powers! And we're covered in motor oil!"
Cozlin rolled her eyes. "This is why I work alone. I don't have to listen to people who complain."

"I wish you were working alone!" Roxy said. "Because then I'd be at home right now! I'm only here because of you. You terrorized Metro City. You dragged me all the way out here. You said it was fine to go through that energy shield. And now I'm covered in motor oil!"
Cozlin folded her arms. "You already complained about that part."
"Grr!" Roxy stamped her foot.
Cozlin frowned. "Let's just figure out how to get out of here."
"Yes," Roxy said. "And then I'll figure out how to get home."
"Fine," Cozlin said. "I can handle the robots on my own."
"Good," Roxy said. "They're not my problem anyway."
"That's right," Cozlin said. "And if one of them goes to Earth, I won't have to help you. It'll be your problem and not mine."
Roxy remembered what Eldin had said. The robots had taken over every planet they invaded. It was only a matter of time before one arrived on Earth.
She sighed. "You're right. Let's figure out how to get out of here and stop those robots."
They crawled through another tunnel and arrived in a hallway that sloped upward.
"We're heading back to the surface," Roxy said.
Suddenly the walls around them began to shift and change shape. An arm popped out.
Cozlin gulped. "The walls are turning into robots!"
They ran up the hallway as robots stomped after them.
Roxy pointed ahead of them. "There's that energy shield again!"
They ran through the shield, and right away Roxy felt different.
Whiz-hoo! Her eye laser beams blasted a robot that had just stepped through the energy shield.
"Yes!" Roxy cried.
Cozlin grinned as she blasted the next robot. Soon the two heroes had destroyed every robot.
Boom! The wall behind them exploded. They spun around to see a much bigger robot.
"Uh-oh," Cozlin said.
Roxy got ready to fight. Then she heard Cozlin's device beep. The beeping got faster and louder.
"Something is alive here," Cozlin said.
A familiar—but angry—voice came from the robot. "Rocket Girl?"
Roxy scratched her head. "Huh?"
The robot's head opened. Dr. Odd sat inside.
"Why are you here, Rocket Girl?" Dr. Odd asked.
Roxy didn't answer. She was shocked. She was so far from Earth. And Dr. Odd, one of the worst villains from Metro City, was here too!
Cozlin looked from Roxy to Dr. Odd. "You two know each other?"
Roxy nodded. "His name is Dr. Odd, and he's evil."
"I'm not evil anymore!" Dr. Odd shouted. "A judge released me from prison for good behavior!"
Roxy raised an eyebrow. "Good behavior? What did you do that was so good?"
Dr. Odd folded his arms. "I taught technology classes to the other prisoners. I helped them get a decent education."
Roxy snorted. "What were the technology classes about? How to take over a planet with robots?"
"What are you talking about?" Dr. Odd asked.
"Groon used to be a nice planet," Roxy said. "And it looks like you turned it into some sort of robot planet. You did this to other planets too!"
"Yeah!" Cozlin said. "My planet!"
"I didn't do that!" Dr. Odd shouted. He glared at Cozlin. "Who are you anyway?"
Cozlin folded her arms. "I'm Kid Comet."
Dr. Odd pointed to the sphere behind him. "That's my moon. I was living peacefully on it—alone. A magnetic force took control of it and brought me here. Now I'm stuck here!"
Roxy narrowed her eyes. "I don't believe you. You're under arrest!"
"You can't arrest me," the villain said. "I didn't do anything, and we're millions of light-years from Earth!"
Whiz-hoo! Roxy's eye laser beams shot toward Dr. Odd. His robot's head snapped shut, hiding him.
Zonk! The robot shot an energy blast at Roxy.
She leaped out of the way as an old spaceship exploded.
Bam! Cozlin punched the robot.
"Gah!" Dr. Odd shouted as the robot nearly lost its balance. It spun around, swinging a huge fist toward Cozlin.
"Yikes!" Cozlin landed next to a big rusty wheel.
Zonk! An energy blast flew toward her.
Cozlin quickly stepped through the wheel. Boom! She appeared on the other side as the blast hit an old rocket. The robot fired another energy blast. The wheel exploded.
Roxy quickly knocked the robot over.
"Argh!" Dr. Odd shouted.
Pow! Cozlin slammed into the robot's side.
The robot's leg swung, kicking Cozlin.
Cozlin went tumbling into a pile of twisted scrap metal. As she struggled to get free, an arm grabbed her ankle.
"Ahh!" Cozlin shouted. "This metal is turning into more robots!"
Roxy flew over and grabbed her wrist.
"Don't worry!" Roxy said. "I'll get you out of there!"
Orange beams radiated from her eyes. Slowly the robots and all the metal began to melt. Roxy pulled Cozlin free as the pile melted into a large puddle.
Roxy looked around. "Where did Dr. Odd go?"
Cozlin shrugged. "I don't know. But we need to get off this planet and form a new plan. We can't handle this alone."
Roxy folded her arms. "Oh! Sounds like Kid Comet needs even more help now."
Cozlin rolled her eyes. "Let's just go back to my ship."
But when they got to the spaceship, both superheroes gasped.
"Your ship!" Roxy said. "The robots took it apart!"
Roxy groaned. "We're stuck on this robot planet!"
Cozlin looked around. Broken spaceships lay everywhere. But none looked like it would still fly. She looked at Dr. Odd's moon. "Do you think Dr. Odd has something we can use?"
Roxy was confused. "He won't let us borrow a spaceship, if that's what you're thinking."
"No," Cozlin said. "But it sounds like we need to arrest him anyway. Maybe he has a spaceship in that moon."
Roxy sighed. Cozlin had a point. Dr. Odd was probably their best chance of getting off this planet.
They flew to the moon and opened a hatch. Quietly they walked down a hallway. They arrived at a big door, and Cozlin's device beeped quickly.
"I'm detecting life," Cozlin said. "Dr. Odd is behind this door."
Roxy fired her eye laser beams. Whiz-hoo! The door exploded, and the two superheroes burst into the room.
Dr. Odd was drinking a cup of tea. He held up his hands. "Stop! Don't destroy anything!"
Roxy was surprised. She expected him to fight.
"Please," Dr. Odd said. "If we fight in here, my computer controls will all get destroyed. Then none of us will ever leave this planet."
Roxy gave him a suspicious look.
Dr. Odd held up his hands again. "I'm unarmed. My big robot is in its charging station. So please, just listen to me."
Roxy folded her arms. Cozlin did the same.
"Okay," Roxy said. "Talk."

Dr. Odd took a deep breath. "I told you I didn't harm this planet, and I was telling the truth." He held out his arms. "This is my moon. I spent years designing it, and my robots built it while I was in prison. All I wanted was to travel around the galaxy and explore—by myself. But then a magnetic force dragged me here, to Groon."
"What happened to Groon?" Cozlin asked. "Where are all of its forests?"
"Robots buried all the forests under layers of metal and machinery," Dr. Odd said.
Roxy narrowed her eyes. "How do you know that?"
Dr. Odd turned on a computer. "I found this computer deep in the planet while exploring one day. Watch this."
A video showed a small city surrounded by lush forests. Roxy saw that the aliens in the video looked happy.
"This is a Groonian city," Dr. Odd said.
